data.description:
## Context / Problem

Epic 62dc's criteria 2, 3 and 4 are undelivered: `rebar create` does not surface semantically similar existing tickets, so agents re-file work that already has a ticket. ADR 0122 (`docs/adr/0122-similar-ticket-retrieval.md`, Accepted 2026-10-31) settled the architecture by measurement and is the binding design record; this ticket is the container for building what it specifies.

The create-time advisory that exists today is a same-title journal only: `duplicate_create_warning` (`src/rebar/_commands/recent_creates.py:117`), gated by `verify.suggest_duplicate_tickets` (`:129`), matching on `title_norm` equality (`:103`). It catches byte-identical normalized titles and nothing else. ADR 0122 measured that stratum at 93.9% of recorded duplicate pairs and ruled a pooled score inadmissible; the 93 differing-title semantic pairs are what this work exists to catch, where the chosen `vector` architecture reaches recall@5 0.876 against the `fts5` baseline's 0.823 (p=0.0213).

ADR 0122 also records a deployment precondition that gates this work: the digest and the embedding run under different Bedrock model families, and `infra/terraform/iam_s7.tf` admits Anthropic Claude only, so the embedding call is denied in any deployed environment until the resource list is widened.

## Approach

Build the index exactly as ADR 0122's Architecture section specifies, then surface it through the advisory-field seam that `duplicate_warning` already proves end to end, rather than introducing a second create-time notification path. That seam carries an optional advisory on the same create result across all three surfaces — library and MCP as a result key (`src/rebar/types.py:276`, `src/rebar/_lib_writes.py:179`), CLI on stderr so stdout stays pure (`src/rebar/_commands/composer.py:467`) — and is already described in `src/rebar/schemas/create_result.schema.json`. Reusing it means the three-surface parity requirement is met by extending a path that already has parity, not by building one.

Sequencing is driven by the riskiest assumption rather than by layering. The assumption most likely to sink this work is not the retrieval quality — ADR 0122 measured that — but whether the Titan embedding call is reachable from the deployed role at all. That is why the IAM widening is the first child and a hard prerequisite of the others: it is cheap, it is falsifiable immediately, and building the index first would mean discovering the denial after the expensive work is done.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `rebar create` returns the top 5 similar existing tickets (id, alias, title, score) as an advisory field on all three surfaces — CLI `--output json`, the library `create_ticket` return dict, and MCP `create_ticket` — within a p95 of 500 ms on a synthetic store of at least 10,000 tickets when the index is warm. Checked by: the three-surface parity tests plus a timing test that asserts the generated store's size rather than assuming it.
- [ ] No derived search data is written to the `tickets` branch: after 100 creates and 100 reads against a test store, the branch contains only user event types. Checked by: an integration test asserting the event-type set of the branch after the run.
- [ ] A ticket created on a clone is findable by the next `create` on that same clone with no background process, daemon, MCP server or CI involved, via read-phase catch-up. Checked by: an integration test that runs the two creates in one process with no daemon, plus the measured cold-catch-up p95 recorded on this ticket (epic criterion 2's 500 ms bound is scoped to a warm index and does not cover this path).
- [ ] Retrieval degrades to advisory-empty and never blocks a create: when the index is absent, catch-up fails, Bedrock denies or errors, or the digest parse yields empty fields, the create still succeeds and the advisory field is empty or lexical-only with a diagnostic. Checked by: one test per failure mode asserting the create's exit status and the advisory contents.

## Child decomposition

- **Bedrock IAM widening for the Titan embedding model** — delivers the deployment precondition ADR 0122 names. A prerequisite of both children below: until it lands and is applied, the embedding call is denied outside a developer's own credentials.
- **The retrieval index subsystem** — digest, embedding, persistence, dir-hash freshness key, incremental catch-up, and the empties/retry counters ADR 0122 requires of any consumer. Delivers criterion 3 and the catch-up mechanism criterion 4 depends on, and the degradation behaviour of criterion 4's failure modes.
- **Create-time surfacing across the three surfaces** — extends the existing advisory-field seam, and carries the parity, timing and branch-purity measurements. Delivers criteria 1 and 2, and criterion 4's end-to-end check.
data.title: Index and create-time surfacing for similar tickets (ADR 0122)
